final.memo:
The environment has shifted significantly. We have moved from a period of finding abundant, undervalued securities to one where the market is dominated by speculative, performance-oriented participants [D01]. With the 10-year Treasury yielding 6.56% against an earnings yield of only 5.75% for the S&P 500, the arithmetic of common stocks currently offers no margin of safety for the risks involved [D04]. 

At our current scale, we require ideas that can move the needle—meaning commitments of approximately $3 million or more [D03]. Such opportunities have become increasingly scarce, and our recent experience with workouts has been unsatisfactory [D03]. Attempting to force investments in this climate would likely require abandoning our core competence or accepting substandard returns [D05], [D07]. Consequently, the most prudent path for our partners is to return capital rather than persist with a strategy that has lost its footing [D05], [D08].
